title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: WENDELL'S MIC
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Wendell Price, a water meter reader from Sacramento, California.
For thirty years, he was the funniest guy at the water department.
But he had never told a joke to strangers.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE SIGN-UP SHEET
segments.quote: You've got to jump off the cliff all the time and build your wings on the way down.
segments.author: Ray Bradbury
lines: One Tuesday, his wife Bernice showed him a flyer. Open mic comedy night at Rusty's Bar.
Wendell said, Maybe next year. He'd said that for twenty years.
Bernice taped up a line from Ray Bradbury, the science fiction writer:
You've got to jump off the cliff all the time and build your wings on the way down.
So he signed up. In very small letters.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: ONE COUGH
segments.quote: This thing that we call failure is not the falling down, but the staying down.
segments.author: Mary Pickford
lines: Night one, Wendell forgot his first joke. Then his second.
Five minutes. One cough. That was his whole review.
Outside, Rosa the bartender quoted Mary Pickford, the silent movie star:
This thing that we call failure is not the falling down, but the staying down.
Next Tuesday, he was back. Same shaky knees.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE FROG
segments.quote: Humor can be dissected, as a frog can, but the thing dies in the process.
segments.author: E. B. White
lines: He studied comedy like a tax return. One pie joke, rewritten forty times.
The jokes got perfect. And nobody laughed.
Rosa slid him a napkin with words from E. B. White:
Humor can be dissected, as a frog can, but the thing dies in the process.
So he stopped dissecting, and just told stories, like he did at work.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE HECKLER
segments.quote: The greatest remedy for anger is delay.
segments.author: Seneca
lines: His stories about dogs and sprinklers got laughs.
Then a man in the back yelled, Boring! Go read a meter!
His face went hot. Then he remembered Seneca, the Roman thinker:
The greatest remedy for anger is delay.
He sipped his water, counted to three, and said, Sir, I already read yours. You owe ninety bucks.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE NOTEBOOK
segments.quote: The most wasted day of all is that on which we have not laughed.
segments.author: Nicolas Chamfort
lines: After that, Wendell carried a little notebook on his route.
Every day, one funny thing. A goose chasing the mailman.
On page one, he copied a line from Nicolas Chamfort, a French writer:
The most wasted day of all is that on which we have not laughed.
He never wasted another one.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE BIG NIGHT
segments.quote: If you work really hard, and you're kind, amazing things will happen.
segments.author: Conan O'Brien
lines: In spring, Rusty's gave him the Saturday closing spot.
Backstage, he helped a nervous young comic named Devon.
Bernice squeezed his hand and quoted Conan O'Brien, the late night host:
If you work really hard, and you're kind, amazing things will happen.
Wendell brought the house down. So did Devon.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Jump. Get back up. Stop dissecting. Wait. Laugh daily. Work hard, be kind.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Jump. Get back up. Stop dissecting. Wait. Laugh every day. Work hard, and be kind.
I tried stand-up once. Turns out I'm better at sit-down.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
